sentence_stem: If I had studied harder last year,
correct_completion: I would be in a better job now.
full_sentence: If I had studied harder last year, I would be in a better job now.
acceptable_variants: I would be earning more money now.
I would be doing a more interesting job now.

options.text: I was in a better job now.
options.why_wrong: This is a simple past statement without 'would', so it does not express the result of the condition.

options.text: I will be in a better job now.
options.why_wrong: After an 'if' clause in the past perfect, the main clause uses 'would' rather than 'will'.

options.text: I would be in a better job now.
I would have been in a better job last year.
options.why_wrong: This is a third conditional about the past, but the sentence needs a present result, so 'now' is required.

grammar_focus: Mixed conditionals: a past condition with a present result
explanation: Mixed conditionals combine a past condition (if + past perfect) with a present result (would + base verb). Learners sometimes use 'will' in the main clause, but after a past perfect if-clause the main clause uses 'would'. Turkish speakers often find the time mismatch between the two clauses confusing, so it helps to label each clause as past or present.
translation: Geçen yıl daha çok çalışsaydım, şimdi daha iyi bir işte olurdum.
